title: Free 12 Months Google AI Pro (5TB Storage) Trial Extension for Eligible University Students @ Google
body:

[safrane] You cannot ace a Uni exam with just AI. Even with open book exams if you don't truly memorise and understand the concepts taught, you'll never be able to finish the exam in time because they're intentionally short on time so you don't have time to regurgitate your notes. And it's very difficult to not get caught with AI anti-cheat with assignments.
What AI is really good at is to explain the teachings, generate notes, test your knowledge, generate problem questions and pick your brain. It augments your learning.
And once you enter the workforce you're expected to know how to use AI, because it's going to get shoved down your throat whether you like it or not.
[netsurfer] Other students are already on ChatGPT and Claude drugs and those are paid drugs. This is free drug for a year so don't expect it to be as good.
[BestTechAdvisor] Gemini Notebook (previously Notebook LM) is a genuine learning tool. It's not just AI slop. It's not just a tool for cheating.
You can use it to gather trusted sources of truth and create study exercises from there, such as flash cards.
[Koppeldread] As someone who did my first masters pre-ai and is now doing a second one, It is brutally hard to maintain the discipline without AI when it is just there begging you to use it. Especially when you know all your competition is using it and test difficulty is scaled up to accommodate AI use…
You start out just using it to summarize a text, then paraphrase a sentence, the to help you with your reference list. Then suddenly you are at the bottom of the slippery slope asking for three separate 1200 word essays on the topic that mimic your writing style.
[BestTechAdvisor] @Koppeldread: Yeah, any tool can be misused, but Notebook is a genuine learning tool, and any certification worth its weight will require to prove your knowledge.
AI's not really the problem, the testing is. Starting next year, HSC students will have a max of one take-home assignment worth up to 15% of the school-based assessment for each subject. Massive improvement.

[SlowCarSlow] @netsurfer: Honestly I haven't really seen a use case for this stuff for an individual for non-commercial purposes that I myself would want.
[netsurfer] @SlowCarSlow: Students - they just take a photo of the homework paper or assignment on the phone, without typing a word, AI starts to do it. ChatGPT offered it since the very beginning I think (but limited to paid version from memory).
For general public, even the free version of AI, essentially gives you free OCR. I think a year ago, I had to fill in a form someone sent me via whatsapp, the image wasn't that great (wouldn't print out well). Upload it and AI converted it to a digital version for me.
My boss can generate infographic for his presentations using AI very quickly. His presentations nowadays are pretty much done by AI.
There was one report a client asked me to do and he wanted it right away (like within an hour). AI did it for me (I didn't let the client know AI did it). If I were to do that myself manually, it would take a day.
There are so many advanced usage but they are complicated for most people. Put it this way, if you are using AI properly, your general view would be paid AI is good value for money.
[entropy47] @netsurfer: Glad to hear it's also useful for performing OCR when people send me forms over WhatsApp as low quality images, but I still think I'll pass.
Bit of a worry if it can do your job to the same quality as you in less time. I wouldn't mention that to your AI-pilled boss or he might make a slop infographic about a new cost cutting opportunity.
[netsurfer] @entropy47: The skills that AI needed to generate the report were provided by me. Without those skills, AI wouldn't be able to do the report.
The report required gathering a lot of data and running a whole bunch of tasks. AI can do them in parallel, monitor each sub-task before combining the final data. While AI was doing that, I was working on something else.
OCR example, I tried Photoshop first. After about 3 minutes, I found it frustrating because some of the texts are so blurry. AI did a great job converting it to digital, those blurry texts, AI had no issue recognise them. I had better things to do than re-type that form.
You need to know what AI is capable of to know when you will get replaced. AI did the report, but I designed it. When I have time, I will have AI re-tune that report as I reckon I will need to generate similar reports for other clients. Also, next time, I will be able to just run this new report generator without asking AI every single time. If AI can replace you, then you will get replaced.
[netsurfer] @SlowCarSlow: In workplaces, people who really know (or those high paid contractors) are the ones using AI the most (and they have been doing that for quite some time now). Ask one of them to show you, you will be impressed.

You do get to use a bit of Claude Sonnet and Opus with Pro (not in Plus), but the number of tokens you get for those is a joke. If you really want to use Sonnet or Opus, get Claude. Pro also has GPT-OSS, but that model is rubbish.
Google know it doesn't need to be number 1 in AI benchmarks. Most of us either have an Android or an iPhone or both and we use a lot of Google products (Google Search, youTube, and maybe GMail).
Would love to be able to get this offer (but I am not eligible). I burn through AI tokens too quickly and I don't like to use dumb LLM models. You end up spending more time correcting their mistakes or getting frustrated.

[netsurfer] More than you think. Not just companies and governments. Don't be surprised if majority of university students use paid AI services.
Most of us are under utilising AI. The younger generation now get to use AI for their studies so they know when you feed data you want AI to do for you, what it is capable of. When you give AI enough context and give it a set of rules so it doesn't drift or waste time working out what's required, it can accomplish tasks really well and often exceeds expectations. You only have 2 hands, you cannot type faster than AI can.
No longer need to read the whole textbook to get the key points of the book is changing the playing field. Sure, if you are gunning for the top 1-5%, you probably still need to read the book. But if you are someone who struggle to read books, AI is narrowing that gap for you. If you are not working in a tech related industry, then AI's impact AI is probably still low. If you work in tech, using AI can and is having a large impact.
